description.value: The study investigated impaired cognitive control and associated brain activation differences during a manual Stroop task in individuals with methamphetamine dependence compared with healthy controls, and examined relationships between activation, accuracy, drug-use characteristics, and impulsivity.

design.value: A case-control fMRI study with 18 individuals with methamphetamine dependence and 21 healthy controls performing congruent and incongruent conditions of a manual Stroop test. Functional activation was analyzed using a group-by-condition ANCOVA with age as a covariate, followed by behavioral and correlational analyses.

clinical_characteristics.value: MA abusers reported MA consumption for approximately 15.3 years (SD = 6.1) on average, with a mean age of 17.8 years (SD = 4.0) when beginning the first MA consumption. At the time of measurement, methamphetamine abstinence existed for an average of 8.3 ± 6.4 days. The crystal meth was administrated mostly in an intranasal way and approximately on 16.9 days out of the last 30 days.

clinical_characteristics.value: Control subjects did not report any cannabis consumption. Both groups reported irregular alcohol consumption with a median of 1×/week.

education_summary.value: Control subjects had a median of 12 years schooling.

task_description.value: The manual version of the Stroop test consisted of two conditions: a congruent (CC) and an incongruent condition (IC). In the CC, 18 color words were presented in the color denoted by the corresponding word; in the IC, 18 color words were displayed in one of three colors, which were not denoted by the word. Two possible answers were presented, and subjects indicated as fast as possible the type of color by pressing one of two buttons.

presentation_software.value: Presentation software (Neurobehavioral Systems Inc., Albany, California)

instructions.value: All subjects were instructed to indicate as fast as possible the type of color by pressing one of two buttons (with right index or middle finger), which corresponded spatially to both possible answers.

stimuli.value: 18 color words in each condition; congruent words were presented in the color denoted by the word, whereas incongruent words were displayed in one of three colors not denoted by the word. Two possible answers in black type were presented in the lower visual field.

task_description.value: A resting-state fMRI was acquired to investigate putatively altered functional connectivity (not reported here).

instrument.value: MAGNETOM PRISMA FIT, Siemens Healthineers, Erlangen, Germany, 3 T whole body system equipped with a 64-element head matrix coil

description.value: A series of 220 whole-brain volume sets were acquired in one session. T2*-weighted images were obtained using a multiband multislice GE-EPI sequence with 104 contiguous transverse slices covering the entire brain and including the lower brainstem. The matrix size was 160 × 160 pixels with an in-plane resolution of 1.4 × 1.4 mm².

description.value: High-resolution anatomical T1-weighted volume scans (MP-RAGE) were obtained in sagittal orientation with a field of view of 256 × 256 mm², a matrix of 256 × 256, 192 sagittal slices, acceleration factor PAT = 2, and isotropic resolution of 1 × 1 × 1 mm³.
A resting-state fMRI was acquired to investigate putatively altered functional connectivity (not reported here).

The functional images were slice-time corrected and corrected for head motion. The structural T1 image was adjusted for intensity non-uniformity and non-brain tissue was removed. Functional images were co-registered to the T1 reference using boundary-based registration, T1 images were normalized to MNI space using nonlinear registration, and the functional images were normalized and spatially smoothed with a 6 mm FWHM Gaussian kernel.

steps.value: The functional images were slice-time corrected using 3dTshift from AFNI.
The functional images were corrected for head-motion.
Structural T1 image was adjusted for intensity non-uniformity.
Functional images were co-registered to the T1 reference using bbregister (FreeSurfer), which implements boundary-based registration.
T1 images were normalized to MNI space by applying nonlinear registration using ANTs version 2.2.0.
The derived transformation parameters were used to normalize the functional images.
Functional images were spatially smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of 6 mm FWHM using mcflirt (FSL 5.0.9).
The first four images were discarded.

model_settings.value: The data were high-pass filtered with a cutoff period of 128 s, corrected for serial correlations choosing AR(1), and analyzed voxel-wise to calculate statistical parametric maps of t statistics for condition specific effects.

A between-subjects factor group (MA vs HC), a within-subjects factor task (CC vs. IC), and age as a covariate were included. Whole-brain group comparisons were thresholded at voxel-level p < 0.001 uncorrected with a minimum cluster size of k ≥ 16. Clusters were also assessed using FWE correction for multiple comparisons at p < 0.05.
One between-subjects factor group (MA vs. HC) and one within-subjects factor condition (CC vs. IC) were used for reaction time.
Group differences in the number of correct responses were analyzed non-parametrically.

Correlations were performed between Stroop accuracy and mean parameter estimates from significant clusters in the IC contrast HC vs. MA, and between those parameter estimates and duration of drug consumption, age of starting crystal meth consumption, and the UPPS total score.
